Report_ID: Non-fatal myocardial infarction (time-to-first-event hazard ratio) — NOT REPORTED
Title: Long-term study of patients with type 2 diabetes and moderate renal impairment shows that dapagliflozin reduces weight and blood pressure but does not improve glycemic control
Author: Kohan DE, Fioretto P, Tang W, List JF
Comment: NOT POOLABLE. No hazard ratio, confidence interval, or event counts for non-fatal myocardial infarction are reported. The only MI data are FATAL MIs listed as causes of death (placebo: 2 acute MI plus 1 MI with cardiac failure/renal failure; dapagliflozin 5 mg: 2 MI with cardiac arrest; dapagliflozin 10 mg: 1 MI), which are explicitly excluded by the synthesis plan (fatal MI must not be pooled). No numeric effect fields were filled; nothing was reconstructed from counts.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Dapagliflozin 5 mg + 10 mg (pooled SGLT2 inhibitor arms)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 2/3 trial
domain: nephrology / endocrinology (type 2 diabetes with moderate renal impairment)
Country: Multinational (USA, Argentina, Canada, India, Mexico, Peru, Italy, Australia, France, Spain, Denmark, Puerto Rico, Singapore; 111 sites)
Participant type: Adults (≥18 years) with type 2 diabetes mellitus, HbA1c 7.0-11.0%, and moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59 ml/min per 1.73 m2)
Recruitment source: 111 clinical trial sites across 13 countries; enrolled 19 June 2008 to 21 May 2009 (NCT00663260 / Study MB102029)
Outcome measurement: Myocardial infarction mentioned only within the narrative list of causes of the 10 deaths through 104 weeks (i.e. fatal MI); no non-fatal MI counts and no hazard ratio reported anywhere in the paper
Outcome variable: Non-fatal myocardial infarction (time-to-first-event hazard ratio) — NOT REPORTED
additional_group_ns: Dapagliflozin 5 mg n=83; dapagliflozin 10 mg n=85; placebo n=84 (arms would need pooling, but no non-fatal MI data exist in any arm)

Report_ID: MACE (adjudicated major adverse cardiac events) — closest reported proxy for non-fatal myocardial infarction; counts only
Title: Safety and Effectiveness of Bexagliflozin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Stage 3a/3b CKD
Author: Allegretti et al.
Comment: The paper reports NO hazard ratio (and no confidence interval, test statistic or p value) for myocardial infarction, and does not report non-fatal MI as a separate outcome — only the composite adjudicated MACE as event counts (2 vs 0). Per the synthesis plan, hazard ratios must not be reconstructed from event counts, so this trial cannot contribute a pooled log-HR estimate and should be reported narratively only. The 1.3% / 0% figures are the paper's own percentages, not a computed effect measure.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Bexagliflozin 20 mg once daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: nephrology / endocrinology (type 2 diabetes with stage 3a/3b CKD)
Participant type: Adults ≥20 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, HbA1c 7.0%-10.5%, and eGFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m2 (KDIGO CKD stage 3a/3b)
Recruitment source: 54 investigational sites in the United States, Spain, France and Japan (September 2016 - January 2018)
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of participants with an adjudicated MACE during the 24-week double-blind treatment period (Table 3, Adverse Events by Randomization Status)
Outcome variable: MACE (adjudicated major adverse cardiac events) — closest reported proxy for non-fatal myocardial infarction; counts only

Report_ID: Composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (myocardial infarction reported ONLY within this composite; no standalone non-fatal MI hazard ratio reported)
Title: Canagliflozin and Renal Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes and Nephropathy (CREDENCE)
Author: Perkovic et al.
Comment: CONSTRUCT MISMATCH — DO NOT POOL AS NON-FATAL MI: this paper reports NO standalone hazard ratio (and no standalone event counts) for non-fatal myocardial infarction. The only MI-containing outcomes are the composites "cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke" (HR 0.80, 0.67–0.95) and "cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure or unstable angina" (HR 0.74, 0.63–0.86). Per the synthesis plan, composite MACE, cardiovascular death and stroke must not be pooled as non-fatal MI; this row is recorded only to document the paper's closest reported data and make the exclusion auditable. Any non-fatal MI estimate for CREDENCE would have to come from a supplementary table not contained in the provided text.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Canagliflozin 100 mg once daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults ≥30 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 6.5-12.0%, eGFR 30 to <90 ml/min/1.73 m2 and albuminuria (UACR >300 to 5000), on stable renin–angiotensin system blockade
Recruitment source: 690 trial sites in 34 countries, March 2014 – May 2017
Outcome measurement: Hazard ratio with 95% CI from stratified Cox model; event counts and events per 1000 patient-years
Outcome variable: Composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (myocardial infarction reported ONLY within this composite; no standalone non-fatal MI hazard ratio reported)

Report_ID: Major cardiovascular events (composite) — NOT non-fatal myocardial infarction alone
Title: Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (EMPA-KIDNEY)
Author: EMPA-KIDNEY Collaborative Group (Herrington WG, Staplin N, et al.)
Comment: CONSTRUCT MISMATCH — DO NOT POOL AS NON-FATAL MI: this paper's own text does not report a hazard ratio (or event counts) for non-fatal myocardial infarction. The only related statistic available in the provided text is the composite 'major cardiovascular events' HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.76-1.12); the MI component is referenced only in supplementary Tables S5/S6, which are not included in this PDF text. Recorded for auditability of the exclusion decision. Also note the trial enrolled CKD patients with OR without diabetes (46.2%/45.8% with any diabetes, ~96% of those type 2), i.e. not a type-2-diabetes-only population. Follow-up: median 2.0 years (IQR 1.5-2.4).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults with chronic kidney disease (eGFR 20-<45, or 45-<90 with urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio >=200), with or without diabetes
Outcome measurement: Hazard ratio for empagliflozin vs placebo from Cox model adjusted for age, sex, history of diabetes, eGFR, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio and geographic region
Outcome variable: Major cardiovascular events (composite) — NOT non-fatal myocardial infarction alone
